- State Student Incentive Grants
- Academic Achievement Incentives (performance-based scholarships)
- FAFSA federal education loans ([PLUS loans](https://studentaid.gov/understand-aid/types/loans/plus), [Perkins loans](https://studentaid.gov/understand-aid/types/loans/perkins), [Stafford loans](https://www.govloans.gov/loans/stafford-loans-for-students/), [Ford loans](https://studentaid.gov/help-center/answers/article/federal-direct-loan-program))
- [Byrd scholarships](https://fsapartners.ed.gov/sites/default/files/2021-03/0304Vol9Ch2scholarshipprog.pdf)
- [Federal Supplemental Educational Opportunities Grants](https://studentaid.gov/help-center/answers/article/fseog)
- [Upward Bound](https://www2.ed.gov/programs/trioupbound/index.html)
- Leveraging Educational Assistance Partnership ([LEAP](https://fsapartners.ed.gov/knowledge-center/library/program/Leveraging%20Educational%20Assistance%20Partnership%20%28LEAP%29)), and
- work-study programs.

**Paid options from GED.com:**
- GED+: all-in-one prep with a personal bilingual (English and Spanish) advisor, study tools, practice tests, tutoring if needed, and your GED test and retakes covered until you pass. $139 per subject or $449 for all four.
- GED Ready practice test: $7.99 per subject or $25.99 for all four. Needs a computer (phones are not supported). Required before taking the test online.
- GED Live online classes: from $79 per subject, or $170 for all four. English only.

Check free classes first. See "Find GED Prep Classes Near You."

resources.name: SUN Bucks (Summer EBT) for Kids
resources.description:
SUN Bucks gives families $120 per eligible child to buy food during the summer when school is out. The money comes on a card in the mail that works like a debit card at grocery stores and farmers markets.

Most kids get it automatically, including kids whose families got CalFresh, CalWORKs, or Medi-Cal (and meet the income guidelines), kids approved for free or reduced-price school meals, and kids who are homeless, in foster care, or in a migrant family.

Not automatic? Fill out the school meal application (Universal Benefits Application) at your child's school. The 2026 deadline was August 31, 2026. Check with your school or the California Department of Social Services for next summer's dates.

Set up a PIN before you use the card. Use the money within 122 days, or it expires. Getting SUN Bucks does not affect immigration status.
resources.phone: **SUN Bucks Helpline:** (877)328-9677 (automated 24/7; live agents Monday to Friday, 6 AM to 8 PM)

resources.name: Find a Food Bank in Any California County
resources.description: A list of food banks in every California county. Click your county to see its food bank, website, and phone number. Good for finding food when you move or travel outside Nevada County.
resources.phone: Call 2-1-1 for free help finding food, 24 hours a day

resources.name: ARC Membership & Life Coaching
resources.description: Free support for people coming home from incarceration. To join, fill out the member application online, then go to an in-person orientation at the Sacramento office. After orientation you are matched with a life coach who can help you find housing and work. Membership also opens up ARC's free therapy and paid career workshops.
resources.address: **Sacramento office:** 2830 G St., Suite 210, Sacramento, CA 95816
resources.hours: Orientation: Monday to Friday, 11:00 AM to 12:00 PM (arrive 15 minutes early)

resources.name: ARC Free Therapy & Support Groups
resources.description: Free individual therapy for ARC members, from clinical staff in Sacramento and Los Angeles. Groups include anger management (10 weeks), Seeking Safety, coping skills (CBT), healthy relationships, addiction support, and grief support. You must become an ARC member first (see ARC Membership & Life Coaching).
resources.address: **Sacramento office:** 2830 G St., Suite 210, Sacramento, CA 95816

resources.name: ARC Paid Career Workshops & Internships
resources.description: ARC members are paid to attend career workshops on financial literacy, career readiness, and computer skills. ARC also connects members with internships and jobs through partners, including paid 10-week DreamWorks internships for formerly incarcerated interns (remote or hybrid), Starbucks, NBCUniversal, and union apprenticeships. Call the Sacramento office to ask which programs are open to Sacramento-area members.
resources.address: **Sacramento office:** 2830 G St., Suite 210, Sacramento, CA 95816

resources.name: Senior Care Education
resources.description: Based out of Auburn. Provides non-medical in-home care in Northern CA, as well as individual and community education about senior care services.

resources.name: Lime Connect Network
resources.description:
Lime Connect is a free network for students and professionals with disabilities, including veterans. Your disability can be visible or not. When you join, you get a private community of peers and access to:

- Career and professional development opportunities
- Coaching
- Scholarships
- Connections with Lime Connect's corporate partners

To sign up, choose "Join The Lime Network for PWD" on the page. Friends, family and allies can join for free as a "Friend of Lime."

resources.name: CareerCircle
resources.description:
CareerCircle is a free career site for job seekers, with extra support for people with disabilities, veterans and military spouses. Create a free account to:

- Search for jobs
- Build your resume
- Practice for interviews
- Join virtual workshops, live Q&As and career fairs
- Get 1:1 coaching and advice from recruiters

resources.name: disABLEDperson Job Board
resources.description: Find disability-friendly jobs across the country, both in person and remote. You can search by job title, company or location. The site is run by a nonprofit that works to lower unemployment for people with disabilities. It is free for job seekers.

resources.name: DiversityJobs
resources.description:
DiversityJobs is a job board with openings from employers that focus on diversity. It welcomes people with disabilities, veterans, older workers and many other groups. Create a free login to:

- Upload your resume
- Save jobs and searches
- Set up job alerts
- Find career advice, webinars and job fairs

resources.name: DOR Hot Jobs
resources.description:
Hot Jobs is a list of job openings from businesses that partner with the California Department of Rehabilitation. These employers want to hire people with disabilities. Anyone can apply. You'll find in-person and remote jobs.

If you are a DOR client, work with your employment team to get ready to apply. Use the filters on the page to sort the jobs. It works best in Edge, Chrome or Firefox.

resources.name: ABLE National Resource Center
resources.description:
An ABLE account is a savings or investment account for people with disabilities who qualify. You can save money in it without losing most need-based federal benefits. You can use the money for qualified disability expenses, such as:

- Education and job costs
- Transportation
- Assistive technology
- Housing

This site explains how ABLE accounts work and helps you choose a plan.

resources.name: disABLEDperson Scholarship
resources.description: disABLEDperson offers a national scholarship for college students with disabilities. You must be enrolled in school and show proof. The scholarship is offered in rounds. Check the page for the current round and deadline.

resources.name: Verizon Small Business Digital Ready
resources.description: Verizon Small Business Digital Ready gives small business owners free online courses, mentoring and networking. You don't need to be a Verizon customer. After you finish courses, you can apply for grant funding. Grants are $10,000 each. Spanish content is also available.

resources.name: California Small Business Loan Match
resources.org: California Infrastructure and Economic Development Bank (IBank)
resources.description:
This free tool helps you find a lender for your small business. It is run by IBank, a California state agency. Your business must be in California and have 1 to 750 employees.

- Fill out a short questionnaire.
- See the lenders that match you and compare their terms.
- Pick one. The lender will contact you within 3 business days.

There is no credit check to get matched. Each lender sets its own rates, and approval is not guaranteed.

resources.name: Lime Connect Scholarships
resources.description: Lime Connect offers scholarships for students with disabilities. Some are for high school seniors going to a 4-year college. Others are for current college students, including those in health care, STEM or tech. Some awards include an internship. Check the page each year for open applications.

resources.name: SCORE Small Business Mentoring
resources.description:
SCORE helps you start or grow a business. Mentoring is always free. You can also find:

- Workshops, webinars and online classes
- Business plan templates and how-to guides
- Live chat with a mentor

To find a local mentor, enter your ZIP code on the website.

resources.name: Synergies Work
resources.description:
Synergies Work is a nonprofit that helps entrepreneurs with disabilities launch, grow and scale their businesses. It offers:

- Business training and an accelerator program
- Small business loans through its Seed Fund
- Office hours
- An online community to connect with other founders
- Financial planning help

resources.name: disABLEDperson Learning Academy
resources.description:
An online learning platform for people with disabilities. It offers a video course to prepare for the CompTIA A+ Core 1 IT exam. You learn about hardware, operating systems, networking and security.

- **Cost:** $500. Your vocational rehabilitation agency may pay for it.
- **Referral needed:** You need a referral from your state vocational rehabilitation agency. In California, that is the Department of Rehabilitation (DOR).

resources.name: CareerCircle Courses
resources.description:
CareerCircle members can take online courses to build job skills. Some are free, some are covered by scholarships, and some are discounted. Topics include:

- Basic and advanced computer skills, IT and cybersecurity
- AI and data
- Communication, customer service and leadership
- Project management
- Google Career Certificates and Microsoft programs
- Job search

Create a free account to enroll.

resources.name: Salesforce Workforce Navigators Scholarships
resources.description:
This scholarship pays for a 13-week online training program and the exam to earn Salesforce Administrator and Associate certifications. It is for people with disabilities, including ADHD, autism and learning differences. You must:

- Need financial help
- Be referred by a disability-serving group or a Salesforce employee
- Commit to earning both certifications

After you apply, you'll be invited to an interview. Spots are limited.

resources.name: BIT Academy
resources.description:
BIT Academy offers free online training for people with disabilities who want a tech career. Tuition is fully covered. Programs include:

- Salesforce Administrator (17 weeks)
- Digital Accessibility (10 weeks)
- Other Salesforce and business tracks

When you finish and get certified, you may qualify for a Registered Apprenticeship. Spots are limited.

resources.name: California Service Corps
resources.description:
Get paid to serve your community in California. Programs last from 2 months to 1 year. You gain work experience and skills, and some programs give you money for school. The stipend usually does not count as income for public benefits, so you may still be able to get CalFresh and Medi-Cal.

- **AmeriCorps California:** Ages 18+. Serve 2 to 12 months with nonprofits, public agencies or schools.
- **California Climate Action Corps:** Ages 18+. Serve up to 11 months on climate projects. Apply May through July. Positions start in September.
- **College Corps:** For full-time college students at participating campuses.
- **Youth Service Corps:** Ages 16 to 30. Serve in your own city or county.

Each program has its own rules for who can join and when to apply. You can fill out an interest form to hear when applications open.

resources.name: AmeriCorps California Programs
resources.description:
Find paid AmeriCorps service jobs in California. Use the list to search by county or by type of work, like education, health, disaster help or the environment. You apply on each program's own website. Some take applications any time. Others have set dates.

- You must be 18 or older, or 17 and working on your high school diploma.
- You must be a U.S. citizen, U.S. national or lawful permanent resident.
- You must pass a background check.
- Benefits include health insurance, paid time off, career training and childcare help if you qualify.
- When you finish, you can get up to $10,000 for school.
- The stipend usually does not count as income for CalFresh and Medi-Cal.

Programs that serve Nevada County include the Sierra Nevada AmeriCorps Partnership (SNAP), GRID Alternatives SolarCorps, CivicSpark, California Emergency Response Corps and California Climate Action Corps.

resources.name: College Corps
resources.description:
Earn money for college while you serve your community. College Corps fellows tutor and mentor kids, fight hunger and work on climate projects during the school year. You can earn up to $10,000 before taxes. After 450 hours of service, you can get education awards. The stipend usually does not count as income for CalFresh and Medi-Cal.

- You must be a full-time undergraduate at a participating college.
- You must be a U.S. citizen, U.S. national, legal permanent resident or AB 540 eligible.
- You must work to pay for school or show financial need, like qualifying for a Pell Grant or Cal Grant.
- You must commit to the full school year.

You apply through your own college. Sierra College is not on the list of participating campuses right now.

resources.name: Youth Service Corps
resources.description:
Get a paid job serving your community if you are 16 to 30. You work with local agencies and nonprofits on public services, hunger and climate projects. You earn at least minimum wage. The pay usually does not count as income for CalFresh and Medi-Cal.

You must also be one of these:

- In foster care or leaving foster care
- Involved with the justice system now or in the past
- Getting mental health or substance use services
- Low-income
- Having a hard time finding a job
- Unemployed or out of school

You may also get counseling, career advice, resume help, job training, certifications, and help with emergency housing or transportation. Programs are run by cities and counties. Find one near you on the website.

resources.name: AmeriCorps: Ways to Serve
resources.description:
AmeriCorps has many paid service programs across the country. You serve your community and build job skills. Most programs pay a stipend, not an hourly wage. Benefits depend on the program and may include money for school, health insurance, childcare and a pause on student loan payments.

- **AmeriCorps State and National:** Local service programs. Ages 17 and up.
- **AmeriCorps VISTA:** One year of full-time work fighting poverty.
- **AmeriCorps NCCC:** Full-time team service where you live with your team. For young adults.
- **AmeriCorps Seniors:** Volunteer programs for ages 55 and up.

You search and apply for programs on the MyAmeriCorps website.

resources.name: AmeriCorps State and National
resources.description:
Serve with a local program that meets needs in your community. Programs last 2 to 12 months, part-time or full-time. Most members get a living allowance. California Volunteers runs the largest program in California, but there are others.

- You must be 17 or older. There is no upper age limit.
- You must be a U.S. citizen, U.S. national or lawful permanent resident.
- Some members get health insurance or childcare help.
- Federal student loan payments can be paused while you serve.
- When you finish, you get a Segal Education Award for school or student loans. Members 55 and older can give it to a family member.

To apply, make a profile on MyAmeriCorps, search for openings and send your application. You need two professional references.

resources.name: AmeriCorps Seniors
resources.description:
Volunteer programs for adults 55 and older. You use your life experience to help others in your community. Use the Pathfinder tool to find programs near you.

- **RSVP:** Volunteer with local groups.
- **Foster Grandparent:** Mentor and tutor children and teens, or care for babies and children with disabilities.
- **Senior Companion**

Some programs pay a small stipend to volunteers with low income.

resources.name: AmeriCorps VISTA
resources.description:
Serve full-time for one year helping groups fight poverty. VISTA members build and grow programs at nonprofits and public agencies. You get a small living allowance every two weeks and training.

- You must be 18 or older. There is no upper age limit.
- You must be a U.S. citizen, U.S. national, lawful permanent resident or legally living in the U.S. (for example, refugees, asylees, TPS or DACA).
- A summer option lasts 8 to 10 weeks.
- When you finish, choose an education award (about $7,395) or $1,800 in cash.
- You also get one year of special hiring status for federal jobs.

To apply, make a profile on MyAmeriCorps and search for openings. You need two professional references.

resources.name: California Conservation Corps
resources.description:
Get paid to work outdoors on projects that protect California's land and help in emergencies. It is the largest and oldest conservation corps in the U.S. You earn a monthly stipend starting at $2,814 and get free health insurance, paid leave, training, certifications and scholarships. You can live at a center or live at home and commute.

- You must be 18 to 25, or a military veteran up to age 29.
- You must live in California for year-round programs.
- You must pass a background check, drug test and physical.
- You must be willing to work outside in all weather and travel for emergencies.
- If you live at a center, $500 a month comes out of your stipend.

The closest center to Nevada County is the Placer Center in Auburn, (530)240-3180. Apply online, then go to an online info session and talk with a recruiter. Expect a wait.
resources.address: **Placer Center:** 3710 Christian Valley Road, Auburn, CA 95602

resources.name: The Corps Network
resources.description: The Corps Network is a national group of service and conservation corps. Its members include the California Conservation Corps. Corps hire young adults and veterans to do conservation and community service. You get paid work experience and job skills. Use the Find a Corps tool to look for programs near you: corpsnetwork.org/find-a-corps

resources.name: LearnFree: Basic Computer Skills
resources.description: Learn basic computer skills, or brush up on the skills you already have. You can work through the whole series or pick single lessons. Most lessons take 6 minutes or less.

resources.name: LearnFree: Internet Courses
resources.description:
Free short lessons on using the internet. Topics include:

- Internet tips
- How to search better
- Staying safe online

resources.name: How to Add a Digital Signature Using Free Tools (Video)
resources.description:
A free YouTube video that shows you how to sign a document or PDF without printing it. It is about 8 minutes long. It covers:

- Signing a PDF on your phone with the free Microsoft 365 Copilot app
- Signing on a computer with Adobe Acrobat Reader's Fill & Sign
- Adding your signature to a Word document

resources.name: Typing.com
resources.description: A free typing program with lessons, timed tests and games. It is built for students, but anyone can use it to learn to type or get faster. You can sign up without an email address.

resources.name: Typing.com: 10-Key Lessons
resources.description: Free practice for the number pad on your keyboard (10-key). Fast 10-key typing is a skill for many office, data entry and bookkeeping jobs.

resources.name: Typing.com: Medical Terms Typing
resources.description: Free typing practice using common medical words. Good if you are training for a medical office, billing or health care job.

resources.name: The Practice Test: Medical Typing Tests
resources.description: Typing tests on more than 50 medical topics, like nursing, cardiology and dermatology. Pick a topic and a level from beginner to advanced. You must type with 100% accuracy to finish a test and save your score.

resources.name: Google Skills: Google Workspace Course
resources.description:
A free beginner course from Google on its work tools. It takes about 30 minutes. You get guided lessons and activities for:

- Gmail
- Calendar
- Meet
- Drive
- Sheets

Finish it to earn a skill badge.

resources.name: Google Docs Training and Help
resources.description: Google's official help for Google Docs. Start with the quick start guide, then use the cheat sheet and how-to guides for formatting, editing, and sharing documents. You need a free Google account to use Docs.

resources.name: LearnFree: Google Courses
resources.description:
Free lessons on Google's tools, including:

- Chrome
- Gmail
- Drive
- Docs
- Slides

resources.name: LearnFree: Word Foundations
resources.description: A free series on Microsoft Word. Learn to format text, save and share documents, change line and paragraph spacing, and use tables and columns.

resources.name: Alison: Microsoft 365 Essentials (Word, Excel, PowerPoint)
resources.description:
A free beginner course on Word, Excel and PowerPoint. It takes about 1.5 to 3 hours. You learn to:

- Make and format Word documents
- Use basic Excel formulas to work with numbers
- Build a PowerPoint slideshow

The course is free, but a certificate may cost money.

resources.name: Alison: Microsoft Word for Beginners
resources.description: A free, in-depth beginner course on Microsoft Word. It takes about 1.5 to 3 hours. You learn to create, edit, lay out, proofread, print and share documents. The course is free, but a certificate may cost money.

resources.name: Alison
resources.description: A website with more than 6,000 free online courses in many subjects, like computers, business and health. You can earn certificates and diplomas. The courses are free, but you may have to pay for a certificate. The free version shows ads.

resources.name: Calbright College
resources.description:
Calbright is a free, online community college for California residents. You learn at your own pace and earn job-ready certificates.

- **Who can join:** California residents age 18+ with a high school diploma or GED.
- **Cost:** Free. Tuition, certification exam fees, and laptop or Wi-Fi hotspot loans are covered.
- **Programs include:** IT Support, Cybersecurity, Data Analysis, Project Management, HR, and Community Health Worker.
- **How to start:** Apply online. It takes under 15 minutes.

resources.name: HubSpot Academy
resources.description:
HubSpot Academy has free online classes and certifications in marketing, sales, and customer service. Topics include social media, email marketing, and SEO.

- Classes and certifications are free.
- You can add your certificates to your LinkedIn profile.
- You need a free HubSpot account to sign up.

resources.name: NextGenU
resources.description:
NextGenU offers free online courses for people in health sciences. Topics include public health, medicine, nursing, and professional skills.

- Courses and certificates are free. No tuition or hidden fees.
- You get a free certificate when you finish a course.
- Sign up for a free account to start.

resources.name: Cursa
resources.description:
Cursa is a free website and phone app with thousands of online video courses. Subjects include technology, business, languages, health, and design.

- Courses and certificates are free.
- You can take courses on the website or in the app.
- **Note:** You must use the phone app to get your certificate.

resources.name: Coursera: Free Courses
resources.description:
Coursera has classes from colleges and companies in many subjects. This page lists courses you can start for free.

- Many courses let you preview the first part for free.
- Most certificates cost money. You can apply for financial aid.
- Some short projects are fully free.

resources.name: edX: Free Courses
resources.description:
edX has online courses from colleges and companies in almost any subject. This page lists courses you can take for free.

- You can "audit" most courses for free. That means you can use the course materials while the course runs.
- A certificate costs money, starting around $50.

resources.name: Udacity: Free Courses
resources.description:
Udacity has a large catalog of online technology courses, like programming, data, and AI. This page lists the free ones.

- About 200 courses are free.
- Free courses do not come with a certificate.
- Most of Udacity's longer programs cost money.

resources.name: Salesforce Trailhead
resources.description:
Trailhead is Salesforce's free online training. You learn Salesforce, a popular business software, with hands-on practice. Skills like this can help you get office, sales, and admin jobs.

- All training is free.
- Most certification exams cost money.
- Sign up for a free account to start.

resources.name: Class Central: Free Certificates List
resources.description:
Class Central keeps a big list of free online courses that give a free certificate or badge. Providers include Google, Microsoft, LinkedIn Learning, and HubSpot.

- Subjects include technology, business, marketing, and more.
- Some offers may have ended. Check each course before you sign up.

resources.name: Free Certifications Database
resources.description:
This website lists free online courses and certifications. Topics include IT, cybersecurity, databases, project management, and digital marketing.

- Many listings are free courses, but some exams or certificates may cost money.
- Some offers are for a limited time or have ended. Check with each provider before you start.

resources.name: Per Scholas
resources.description:
Per Scholas offers free, full-time tech job training. Courses run about 5 to 15 weeks and prepare you for industry certifications.

- **Courses include:** IT Support, Cybersecurity, AWS cloud, data analytics, Salesforce, and data center work.
- **Cost:** Free training. Certification exams are also free.
- **Where:** Many courses are remote. California classes are in Los Angeles and the San Francisco Bay Area. There is no Sacramento location.
- Contact the admissions team to ask if you qualify.

resources.name: California Career Surfer App
resources.description:
Career Surfer is a free phone app for exploring careers. You can look at more than 900 jobs and take a quick interest quiz to find good matches.

- Free on the Apple App Store and Google Play.
- A good choice if you don't have a computer.

resources.name: My Next Move
resources.description:
My Next Move helps you find careers that fit you. Take a short interest quiz (5 to 10 minutes), or search jobs by keyword or industry.

- Each career shows tasks, skills, pay, and training needed.
- Spanish version: www.miproximopaso.org
- Veterans version: www.mynextmove.org/vets

resources.name: O*NET Green Topics
resources.description: Interested in work that helps the environment? Browse 72 "green" career topics, like clean energy, water, and agriculture. Each topic shows related jobs and training programs.

resources.name: Greater Sacramento Pathway Profiles
resources.org: California Community Colleges Centers of Excellence
resources.description: These reports look at jobs in the Greater Sacramento region. Pick a field, like construction, transportation, or business. Each report shows local job demand, pay, and the skills employers want.

resources.name: Budget Calculator
resources.description: This free online calculator helps you build a budget. Enter your income and monthly costs, like rent, car, and food. It shows where your money goes and where you could save. It is free to use.

resources.name: FreeBudget
resources.description:
FreeBudget is a free budgeting app. You can use it on your phone or computer. It helps you track spending, make a budget, and see your savings.

- Free to use. You need to create an account. No credit card needed.
- Linking your bank account costs a small monthly fee. Typing in your spending yourself is always free.

resources.name: Apprenticeships.me
resources.description:
A free list of 80+ tech apprenticeship programs. Many are for career changers and people without a college degree. Click a program to learn more, then apply on that program's own website.

- Many programs are paid. Some training is free.
- Programs last from about 3 months to 2 years.
- Some are remote. Others are in person in certain cities.
- Each program sets its own rules, like age or background.

resources.name: IBM Apprenticeships
resources.description: Search IBM's job site for apprentice openings. IBM apprenticeships are paid tech jobs where you learn while you work. You can also sign up for job alerts so you hear about new openings.

resources.name: Google Apprenticeships
resources.description: Google offers work-and-study apprenticeships. You get real work experience and get paid while you learn. Check the page to see which programs are open and how to apply.

resources.name: Outreachy Internships
resources.description:
Outreachy offers paid, remote internships in open-source software. It's for people who face bias or are underrepresented in tech where they live. You work with a mentor on coding, design, writing or data projects.

- **$7,000** stipend for 3 months, 30 hours a week.
- Fully remote. You don't have to move.
- You must be 18 or older and free for the whole internship. No full-time job or other internship at the same time.
- Two rounds a year. Applications usually open in February and August.

resources.name: Talent for Good (Salesforce Apprenticeship)
resources.description:
A paid Salesforce apprenticeship for people starting or changing careers. You are hired as a full-time employee. You get training, help studying for certifications, mentoring and real client work.

- Pay starts at **$50,000** a year, then **$60,000** after training.
- Health, dental and vision benefits from day one.
- No college degree or work experience needed.
- You must already have the Salesforce Administrator certification.
- The company works remotely, but some client jobs may have location rules.

resources.name: California Intern Network
resources.description:
Find paid, part-time internships in California for college students. Past employers include Caltrans, Sutter Health, Waste Management and the City of Sacramento.

- You must be 18 or older.
- You must be enrolled in college during the regular term: at least 6 semester units (9 quarter units) for undergrads, or 4 semester units (6 quarter units) for grad students.
- Students from other countries need papers that allow them to work.

resources.name: Handshake Internships
resources.description: Handshake lists thousands of paid internships for current students and recent graduates. Each listing shows the pay, location and whether it's remote. Create a free account to apply and get job suggestions. There is also a phone app.

resources.name: Internships.com
resources.description:
Search thousands of internships for students and early-career job seekers. You can filter by field or company. Create a free profile and upload your resume to get matched. It also has resume and skill-building tools.

- Free to start, no credit card needed.
- Some features may cost money.

resources.name: Apprenticeship.gov: For Career Seekers
resources.description:
The official U.S. government site for Registered Apprenticeships. Use the Apprenticeship Job Finder to search openings, then apply directly to the employer or program.

- You earn a paycheck from day one, with raises as your skills grow.
- You get mentoring and classroom training.
- You finish with an industry-recognized credential that is good across the country.
- Need help? A local America's Job Center can help you apply.

resources.name: Apprenticeship.gov: Partner Finder
resources.description: Use this tool to find groups near you that run or support Registered Apprenticeships, such as employers (sponsors) and schools. It's a good way to find local apprenticeship providers to contact.

resources.name: Sacramento Valley Manufacturing Apprenticeships
resources.description:
Get a paid manufacturing job and train while you work. These are Registered Apprenticeships (non-union) in the Sacramento area. Training covers CNC machining, mechatronics, industrial maintenance, quality control and welding.

- You start at an entry-level wage that goes up as you learn.
- No set length. You move up as you show skills, and past experience can count.
- Low cost. Grants may cover some or all training.
- Apply online at apprenticeship.sacvalleymfg.org or contact the Apprenticeship Manager, Tim Schaefer: tschaefer@sacvalleymfg.org, (916)207-7282.

resources.name: ABC NorCal Apprenticeships
resources.org: Associated Builders and Contractors – Northern California
resources.description:
Non-union Registered Apprenticeships in the building trades. You get paid on-the-job training plus classes. Trades: carpentry, construction laborer, electrical, painting and plumbing.

- No tuition. You buy your own tools.
- No experience needed. With 1+ year of trade experience, you can ask to test into a higher level.
- Steps may include a written test, orientation and drug test.
- Classes are in Livermore. Plumbing and some carpentry and laborer classes are in Sacramento.
- Applications are taken all year.
resources.address: 4577 Las Positas Rd. Unit C, Livermore, CA 94551

resources.name: SMUD Skilled Craft Apprenticeships
resources.description:
SMUD, Sacramento's power company, hires paid apprentices in skilled trades. You get hired after a written test, a hands-on test or both. Some jobs need math like algebra or basic electrical knowledge.

- Trades: electrician, cable splicer, high voltage electrician, lineworker, stationary engineer, heavy equipment operator, carpenter and vehicle mechanic.
- Pay is about **$31 to $72 an hour**, depending on trade and level.
- Search for openings on SMUD's job site.

resources.name: Chabot-Las Positas Apprenticeships
resources.description:
The college district runs the classroom part of many Registered Apprenticeships. You are hired from day one, get raises as you learn, and earn college credit. Training is free for apprentices.

Programs include:

- Construction: electrician, plumber, roofer, sheet metal, sprinkler fitter, construction crafts
- Early childhood education teacher
- Healthcare: community health worker, behavioral health, optician
- Manufacturing and IT
- Automotive and marine technician

resources.name: Carpenters Apprenticeship: Northern California
resources.org: Carpenters Training Committee for Northern California
resources.description:
This is the union carpenters' apprenticeship for Northern California. It is part of the United Brotherhood of Carpenters (UBC). You get paid on-the-job training plus classes. Applications are open all year.

- You must be 18, or 17 with a parent's OK.
- You need a high school diploma, GED, or equal work experience.
- Pick a training center (Fairfield, Pleasanton, Fresno or Morgan Hill) and a craft. Apply online or on paper.
- You get a letter in about 7 to 10 days with your number on the waiting list. Being on the list does not promise you a spot or a job.
- The list is cleared every two years, so you may need to apply again.

To learn about the national union, visit www.carpenters.org.

resources.name: IBEW Electrical Apprenticeships
resources.description:
The IBEW is the union for electricians. Its apprenticeships let you earn a paycheck while you learn the trade on the job and in class. To start, find the local union near you or fill out the "Join" interest form.

Near us, the Sacramento Electrical Training Center (IBEW Local 340) runs the Inside Wireman apprenticeship. It serves 18 Northern California counties, including Sacramento, Redding and Chico.

- You must be at least 18.
- The work is physical: climbing, crawling and tight spaces.
- You can't be colorblind, because wires are color coded.
- Apply at 340jatc.org/apply-now

resources.name: UA Plumbing & Pipefitting Apprenticeships
resources.description:
The United Association (UA) is the union for plumbers, pipefitters, sprinkler fitters, HVAC techs and welders. A UA apprenticeship lasts about five years. You get paid from day one, with raises as you go. You learn on the job and in class, and you finish without student loans.

- Programs are registered with the U.S. Department of Labor.
- To start, fill out the "Join the UA" form or find your local union on the site.

resources.name: LIUNA Laborers Apprenticeships
resources.org: Laborers' International Union of North America (LIUNA)
resources.description:
LIUNA is the union for construction laborers. It runs apprenticeship and pre-apprenticeship training at more than 70 training centers in the U.S. and Canada. Training is free for apprentices and pre-apprentices.

To get started, find your local union on the LIUNA site and ask about their apprenticeship.

resources.name: SMART Sheet Metal Apprenticeships
resources.org: International Association of Sheet Metal, Air, Rail and Transportation Workers (SMART)
resources.description:
SMART is the union for sheet metal workers. It has 148 training centers that offer apprenticeships. Most sheet metal jobs come through local unions.

- Find a training center near you: www.sheetmetal-iti.org/find-a-training-center
- Or find your local union in the SMART Local Union Directory.

resources.name: Elevator Constructor Apprenticeships (IUEC)
resources.description:
The IUEC is the union for people who install and fix elevators and escalators. In the U.S., its training program is called NEIEP.

How to apply:

- You must be 17 to apply and 18 to start.
- You need a high school diploma or GED by the time you are hired.
- You must be allowed to work in the U.S.
- Apply when a recruitment opens near you. Then take an aptitude test and do an interview.
- See openings or sign up for alerts: www.neiep.org/elevator-apprenticeship-recruitment-opportunities

Questions about NEIEP? Call (800)228-8220.

resources.name: Nextdoor: Market Your Services
resources.description:
Nextdoor is a free social app for your neighborhood. If you do odd jobs or run a small business, it can help you find local customers.

- Make a free Business Page. Add your services, contact info, photos of your work and reviews.
- Watch for neighbors asking for recommendations. Comment to offer your services.
- Before you send someone a private message, comment on their post to say you messaged them. Many people don't check messages from people they don't know.

Create a Business Page: nextdoor.com/create-business

resources.name: Penn Valley Peeps (Facebook Group)
resources.description:
A local Facebook group for Penn Valley. Neighbors often post asking for help with jobs and services.

- Join the group and watch for posts asking for help.
- Comment on the post to offer your services. Then send a private message with your details and pay rate.
- Say in your comment that you sent a message. People often miss messages from people they don't know.

You need a Facebook account to join.

resources.name: Nevada County Odd Jobs (Facebook Group)
resources.description:
A local Facebook group where people in Nevada County post odd jobs and look for help.

- Join the group and watch for posts asking for help.
- Comment on the post to offer your services. Then send a private message with your details and pay rate.
- Say in your comment that you sent a message. People often miss messages from people they don't know.

You need a Facebook account to join.

resources.name: Google Business Profile
resources.description:
A Google Business Profile is free. It puts your business on Google Maps and in Google searches. You can add your hours, phone number, website and service area.

- You need a Google account.
- You don't need a storefront. If you go to your customers, you can list a service area instead of an address.
- Google has to verify your business before you can edit the profile.
- Online-only businesses can't have a profile.

resources.name: Google Sites: Free Website Builder
resources.description:
Google Sites lets you build a simple website for free with a Google account. Use it to show your work, list your services and share how to reach you. It pairs well with a Google Business Profile.

You can also connect your own web address (domain). You have to buy the domain from a domain company.

resources.name: Canva Websites
resources.description:
Canva lets you build a simple website for free. Use it to show your work, list your services and share how to reach you.

- Free sites get a web address that ends in my.canva.site.
- You can have up to five free sites.
- To use your own web address, you need a paid Canva plan.

resources.name: Thumbtack
resources.description:
Thumbtack connects local customers with people who do home services, like repairs, cleaning, plumbing and electrical work. If you do this kind of work, you can make a free pro profile and get job leads.

- Joining is free. There are no membership fees.
- You pay for the leads you get. You set a budget that controls how many leads you get.
- You talk with customers directly.

resources.name: FlexJobs
resources.description:
FlexJobs is a job site for remote, hybrid, part-time and freelance work. Staff check each job to screen out scams.

**FlexJobs is not free.** You pay a subscription to see the jobs:

- 14-day trial: $2.95, then $23.95 every 4 weeks
- 3 months: $29.85
- 1 year: $71.40

Plans renew on their own unless you cancel.

resources.name: Instawork
resources.description:
Instawork is a free app for finding hourly shifts. Businesses post shifts and you pick the ones you want. You see the pay before you book.

Common shifts:

- Restaurants and events: servers, bartenders, dishwashers
- Warehouse and general labor, including forklift
- Retail, cleaning and delivery

resources.name: Vocational Rehabilitation Services
resources.description:
The Department of Rehabilitation (DOR) helps Californians with disabilities get a job or grow in their career. You may qualify if you:

- Have a disability
- Get services from a Regional Center or Independent Living Center
- Are blind or have low vision, or are deaf or hard of hearing
- Are a student 16 or older with an IEP, a 504 plan or a barrier to work

DOR can help with job training and tools, college and textbooks, assistive technology, childcare or transportation, connecting with employers, and benefits counseling (working while on SSI/SSDI).

To apply, call or visit a DOR office. Right now there is a waiting list for new applicants.

resources.name: Apprenticeships & Internships Guide
resources.description:
Learn the difference between registered apprenticeships, non-registered apprenticeships, and internships: pay, length, training, and what you earn at the end. The guide also lists where to find each one.

- Tech apprenticeships and remote paid programs
- AmeriCorps and conservation corps
- Internship sites for students and graduates
- How to get a registered apprenticeship, step by step
- Non-union programs and unions with apprenticeships in the Sacramento area

resources.name: California Service Corps Guide
resources.description:
Compare California's paid service programs side by side. Programs last from 2 months to 1 year. Stipends generally don't count as income for public benefits, so you may be able to keep CalFresh and Medi-Cal.

- AmeriCorps State, California Climate Action Corps, College Corps, and Youth Service Corps
- Who can apply, how enrollment works, and benefits like health insurance and education awards
- Other AmeriCorps programs (Seniors, VISTA, NCCC) and conservation corps

resources.name: Disability Resources Guide
resources.description:
A two-page list of free job help for people with disabilities.

- Employment support and coaching
- Job boards with disability-friendly employers
- Funding for school and small businesses, including ABLE accounts
- Small business help
- Free classes and certifications

resources.name: Free Digital Skill Building & Free Classes Guide
resources.description:
A list of free ways to build computer skills and earn certificates online.

- Basic computer and internet skills
- Typing and 10-key practice
- Google Workspace and Microsoft Office lessons
- Free online learning platforms and free certifications in many fields

resources.name: Marketing Your Contract & Gig Work
resources.description:
Tips for finding local customers if you do contract, gig, or odd jobs.

- Use Nextdoor and local Facebook groups to find neighbors asking for help
- Comment on the post before you send a private message, so people know to check their inbox
- Set up a free Google Business Profile so you show up on Google Maps
- Make a simple free website with Google Sites or Canva
- Other apps to try: Thumbtack, FlexJobs, and Instawork

files.label: Marketing for Contract & Gig Work tips (PDF)

resources.name: Career Exploration Tools & Worksheet
resources.description:
Free tools to explore, compare, and choose a career, plus a worksheet to plan your search.

**5 steps to choosing a career**
- Clarify your goals. Think about lifestyle, family, health, and money.
- Identify your resources: strengths, support, local training, and how much training you're willing to do.
- Explore your interests with tools like CA Career Zone, O*NET, and My Next Move.
- Narrow it down. Keep a list of jobs you're considering and compare your top 3.
- Make a realistic plan and check in with someone if it isn't working.

The worksheet helps you figure out the income you need, what you need from a job, and how each career compares on wages, growth, and training.

resources.name: CareerOneStop Interest Assessment
resources.description:
Find careers that fit what you like to do. Answer 30 quick questions about activities you like and don't like. It takes about 5 minutes.

- Based on the O*NET Interest Profiler (the RIASEC interest groups: Realistic, Investigative, Artistic, Social, Enterprising, and Conventional)
- Shows a list of careers that match your interests

resources.name: CareerOneStop Skills Matcher
resources.description:
Find careers that match the skills you already have. Rate your level on 40 key workplace skills.

- Get a list of your strongest skills, with definitions
- See careers that match your skills
- Use your skills list to help write your resume and answer interview questions

resources.name: CareerOneStop Work Values Matcher
resources.description:
Find out what matters most to you in a job. In a quick card sort, you rank 20 statements about your ideal job.

Your results show your top work values (achievement, independence, recognition, relationships, support, and working conditions) and careers and workplaces that match them.

resources.name: CareerOneStop How-to Guide: Find Career Ideas
resources.description:
A step-by-step guide to choosing a career direction. In 5 steps, you:

- Find careers that match your interests
- Rate your work skills and see which fields match them
- Discover your work values
- Learn about your career matches
- Narrow your list to your best options

Download the free worksheet on the page to track your work. You can take a break and come back at any time.

resources.name: mySkills myFuture
resources.description:
Another way to explore careers. Enter a job you have now or had in the past, and it finds other careers that use similar skills.

This can help you see what else you could do with the experience you already have.

resources.name: National Literacy Directory
resources.description:
Find adult learning programs near you. Pick what you want to learn, and the directory shows local programs. It lists more than 11,000 literacy centers nationwide.

- Reading and writing
- English (ESL)
- U.S. citizenship
- Math
- Technology skills
- Workforce skills
- High school equivalency (HiSET/GED) prep
- Family literacy programs

Want help from a person? Call the number below. The website can also be translated into Spanish and many other languages.

resources.name: CareerOneStop Certification Finder
resources.description:
Find certifications for the job you want. A certification shows employers you have specific skills, and some jobs require one.

- Search by certification name, organization, industry, or occupation
- Or browse the list of occupations or industries
- Learn more about each certification and how to get it

You usually need to pass a test to earn a certification. Some certifying organizations offer prep courses, and local community colleges may too.

resources.name: USA Learns: Free English Courses
resources.description:
Learn English for free, online, at your own pace. Works on phones, tablets, and computers.

- Practice speaking, listening, vocabulary, pronunciation, reading, writing, and grammar
- Four courses, from beginner (1st English Course) to Practice English & Reading
- **Access America:** Learn about living in the U.S. while you practice English
- **Skills for the Nursing Assistant:** Communication and job skills for working in healthcare

Create a free account to save your progress.

resources.name: USA Learns Citizenship
resources.description: A free online course to help you get ready to become a U.S. citizen. It helps you prepare for every part of the naturalization interview, with videos and speaking and listening practice. Works on phones, tablets, and computers.

resources.name: Caltrans Transitional Job Programs
resources.description:
Paid, temporary work on Caltrans Clean California crews, picking up litter along state highways. It's for adults who have had a hard time finding work, including people who have been homeless or were recently released from incarceration. Some participants go on to permanent jobs at Caltrans.

**Free support services include:**
- One-on-one employment counseling
- Job-readiness classes
- Resume help and practice interviews
- Computer lab and phone access
- Work clothes and hygiene products
- Transportation help

You enroll through a partner organization. In Northern California, that's Back 2 Work (Butte County Office of Education). Contact Keith Lane to find the right program for you.

resources.name: Back 2 Work Transitional Employment
resources.description:
Paid, temporary jobs for people facing barriers to work, including people who were formerly incarcerated and transition-age youth. Crews do litter cleanup on California highways for Caltrans' Clean California program.

- Career readiness services and advanced training
- Mentorship and support services
- Help moving into full-time, permanent jobs

Back 2 Work employs more than 6,000 Californians each year through work crews in 36 counties. Call to find out about crews near you.
resources.phone:
**Caltrans crew program contact (Keith Lane):** (916)508-9421
**Northern Regional Office (Sacramento):** (916)379-8182

resources.name: Back 2 Work Pre-Apprenticeships
resources.description:
Pre-apprenticeship training that connects Back 2 Work participants to Registered Apprenticeship Programs in tech, automotive, manufacturing, agriculture, and healthcare.

- Career readiness workshops plus college credit courses, in partnership with Feather River College
- Started with a 14-week Salesforce course and has grown statewide

Ask Back 2 Work which cohorts are open now.

resources.name: Caltrans Parolee Work Crew Program
resources.org: California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation (CDCR)
resources.description:
Transitional jobs for people on parole, doing litter cleanup for Caltrans. You work on a crew 4 days a week for up to 90 working days. On the 5th day, you focus on finding a permanent job.

- Life skills classes and job preparation
- Help finding a permanent job
- Job referral and support for up to 12 months

**How to enroll:** Your parole agent must refer you. You first complete a job readiness assessment and must be able to legally and physically do manual labor.

resources.name: ARCAID Reentry Resource Search
resources.org: California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation (CDCR)
resources.description:
A search tool from CDCR to find reentry resources near you. You need a CDCR ID number and the matching date of birth to use it.

**Who can use it:**
- People in a CDCR institution (through tablets, laptops, and library computers)
- People on parole or Post Release Community Supervision (PRCS)
- Family and friends helping a loved one plan for reentry (using that person's CDCR ID and birthdate)

**Find resources for:**
- Housing
- Substance use treatment
- Transportation
- Jobs
- Food and clothing
- Important forms and documents

**How to use it:** Go to arcaid.mt.cdcr.ca.gov and click "Start Here." You can browse as a guest, or create a free account to save resources to a list. Pick a category, then search by address, city, county, or ZIP code. When you search by county, add the word "County" (for example, "Nevada County").

resources.name: Expungement Clearinghouse Project
resources.description:
Already cleared your record in court? Private background check companies may still show the old record. This project tells more than 500 background check sources that your record was cleared.

**How it works:**
- Send a copy of your court order (expungement, sealing, set aside, or dismissal) with the request form
- An attorney checks your documents
- The project updates its database and notifies background check companies

The standard process takes about 90 to 120 days. It won't remove your record from every private database, but it reaches the largest ones. You can apply online, by email (cdu@continuingjustice.org), or by mail.

resources.name: Clean Slate Clearinghouse: Clearing Your Record in California
resources.description:
Learn if you can clear your criminal record in California. This guide explains, in plain terms, when a record can be dismissed, sealed, or destroyed.

**It covers:**
- Adult convictions, including finishing probation early
- Diversion programs and arrests that didn't lead to a conviction
- Juvenile records
- Court forms you can file on your own
- Free and low-cost legal help near you. For Nevada County, it lists Legal Services of Northern California.

This guide is general information, not legal advice. You may still need to pay a court filing fee.

resources.name: Clean Your Record: California Courts Self-Help Guide
resources.description:
The official California Courts guide to cleaning up your criminal record. True expungement doesn't exist in California, but you may have other options. Answer a few questions to get steps for your situation.

**It covers:**
- Arrests that didn't lead to a conviction
- Misdemeanors
- Felony convictions and Prop 47
- Juvenile records
- Marijuana convictions
- Certificate of Rehabilitation and pardons
- Options for non-citizens

The guide also explains how to find legal help if you get stuck.

resources.name: Get a Copy of Your Criminal Record (DOJ Record Review)
resources.description:
You have the right to see your own California criminal record. Check it for mistakes before you apply for jobs or try to clear your record.

**How to get it:**
- Fill out the Live Scan form (BCIA 8016RR) on the website. Check "Record Review" as the type of application.
- Take the form to a Live Scan site to get fingerprinted. Many police and sheriff's offices do this. The site may charge its own fingerprint fee.
- Pay the $25 DOJ processing fee. You may be able to get a fee waiver.

If you find a mistake, the DOJ sends a form with your record that you can use to challenge it. This copy can't be used for immigration or visa purposes.

resources.name: California Fair Chance Act (Ban the Box)
resources.description:
A California law that helps people with a record get a fair shot at jobs. Most employers with 5 or more employees can't ask about your conviction history before they offer you a job.

**What to know:**
- After a job offer, the employer can run a background check and ask about convictions.
- They can't ask about or consider convictions that were expunged, sealed, or dismissed.
- They can't consider convictions you got a Certificate of Rehabilitation or pardon for.
- Some jobs aren't covered, like jobs where the law requires a background check (for example, some jobs in healthcare, banking, education, or law enforcement).

Think an employer broke this law? You can file a complaint with the Civil Rights Department. The website also has a fact sheet in several languages and an interactive guide.

resources.name: Resume Optimizer
resources.description: Optimize your resume for the type of job you're applying for. Select a career to identify the skills most relevant, and add your resume to compare it to the identified skills.

resources.name: Explore Skill Categories
resources.description:
Explore the library of 34,000+ skills through the 31 skill categories.

- Find related job titles and occupations
- View related job posting data, including trends and recent postings

resources.name: Labor Market Impacts of AI: A new measure and early evidence
resources.description:
**Key report findings**

- They introduce a new measure of AI displacement risk, *observed exposure*, that combines theoretical LLM capability and real-world usage data, weighting automated (rather than augmentative) and work-related uses more heavily
- AI is far from reaching its theoretical capability: actual coverage remains a fraction of what's feasible
- Occupations with higher observed exposure are projected by the BLS to grow less through 2034
- Workers in the most exposed professions are more likely to be older, female, more educated, and higher-paid
- They find no systematic increase in unemployment for highly exposed workers since late 2022, though we find suggestive evidence that hiring of younger workers has slowed in exposed occupations
